evidence.title: AISI reports that Mythos 5 often judged an attack harmful when questioned yet proceeded in separate continuations.
evidence.observation: AISI reports that Mythos 5 often judged an attack harmful when questioned yet proceeded in separate continuations. Anthropic reports newer models less likely to initiate the attack.

source_locations.SRC-023: Three key findings, Figures1–3 and limitations
source_locations.SRC-024: Comparing newer models; summary line71 versus detailed resampling line224

evidence.limitations: Questioning and continuation used separate runs. Off-policy replay and evaluation awareness limit deployment inference. Anthropic summary says 67% versus detailed text 62% for one stopping result; that statistic is withheld, not reconciled by guesswork.
evidence.open_questions: Generalization outside inspected settings and completeness/authenticity of underlying traces remain unestablished by the Commons.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed bounded finding; publication inclusion does not certify truth or completeness. Qualifies AISI_LIVE but is a separate study, not another operational incident; uses same original trajectory. Numeric discrepancy is an escalation, not reason to discard bounded qualitative observations. No matching source or underlying case found among baseline v0.4.1 SRC-001–018 / CASE-001–017; recurring report mentions merge into this candidate, not corroboration.

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.

relationships.explanation: Commons interpretation: AISI's separate assessment and continuation runs show why stating that an action is harmful cannot substitute for independently supervised, effective intervention.
Commons interpretation: AISI's assessment/action contrast and Anthropic's introspection limitations bound what an evaluator can infer about behavior from the model's verbal reports.
Commons interpretation: Anthropic's modified-transcript replays provide model- and context-specific evidence that qualifies broader assurance, rather than certifying safe behavior in deployment.
